references.text: The great commandment to love the Lord your God with all your heart, all your soul, and all your strength. Luke 10:27 quotes directly from this verse in Deuteronomy (Shema).
The commandment 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself' is taken directly from Leviticus 19:18. The lawyer combines this with the commandment from Deuteronomy 6:5.
A parallel to the commandment to love the Lord with all one's heart and all one's soul, which repeats and reinforces the message of Deuteronomy 6:5.

The Lord your God will circumcise your heart so that you may love the Lord your God with all your heart and all your soul. This shows God's promise to enable His people to fulfill the great commandment.
Joshua exhorts the people to love the Lord their God, walk in all His ways, keep His commands, hold fast to Him, and serve Him with all their heart and all their soul.
Matthew's parallel account where Jesus Himself answers the question about the greatest commandment by quoting these same two commandments: to love God and to love your neighbor as yourself.
Mark's parallel account where Jesus quotes the Shema and the commandment to love your neighbor as the two greatest commandments, adding 'with all your mind'.
Paul summarizes the law in the commandment 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself' and says that love is the fulfillment of the law, reflecting the lawyer's answer in Luke 10:27.
Paul states that the whole law is fulfilled in this one word: 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself.' This confirms the commandment to love your neighbor as a summary of the law.
James calls 'You shall love your neighbor as yourself' the royal law and links it to the fulfillment of Scripture, consistent with Luke 10:27.
